title: Community Cooling Center Act
text: The bill requires counties with populations above 100,000 to publish a summer heat response plan. The plan must identify public cooling centers, provide free drinking water during declared heat emergencies, and include transportation options for residents with mobility limitations. The state health department may award grants for equipment and staffing. Counties must submit annual usage reports beginning in 2028.
summary: Requires larger counties to maintain heat response plans with cooling centers, water, and accessible transportation. Authorizes state grants and requires annual usage reporting beginning in 2028.

title: Rural Library Connectivity Act
text: The bill creates a competitive grant program for public libraries in communities with fewer than 25,000 residents. Grants may pay for broadband service, network equipment, cybersecurity training, and public digital literacy classes. Recipients must provide internet access without charge during normal library hours and report expenditures for three years. The program expires on July 1, 2032.
summary: Creates temporary grants for rural public libraries to fund broadband, equipment, cybersecurity training, and digital literacy classes, with free public access and three years of expenditure reports.

title: School Meal Waste Reduction Act
text: The bill directs the education department to issue voluntary guidance for school districts on donating unopened food, establishing share tables, and composting food scraps. Participating districts must follow local health rules and may not reduce required meal portions. The department must publish a statewide implementation report by December 31, 2029. No private right of action is created.
summary: Directs voluntary state guidance on school food donation, share tables, and composting while preserving meal requirements and local health rules. Requires a statewide report by the end of 2029.

title: Small Farm Equipment Safety Credit
text: The bill establishes a refundable income tax credit equal to 30 percent of the cost of approved rollover protection systems and power takeoff shields purchased by farms with annual gross receipts below two million dollars. The credit is capped at 12,000 dollars per taxpayer each year. The agriculture department certifies eligible equipment. The credit applies to tax years 2027 through 2031.
summary: Provides qualifying small farms a refundable tax credit for 30 percent of approved safety equipment costs, capped at $12,000 annually, for tax years 2027 through 2031.

title: Municipal Tree Inventory Act
text: The bill requires cities receiving state urban forestry funds to maintain a public inventory of trees on municipal property. The inventory must record species, approximate age, condition, and removal history, but may omit exact locations of protected or culturally sensitive trees. Cities must update the inventory at least every two years. The natural resources agency may withhold future grants for repeated noncompliance.
summary: Requires recipients of state urban forestry funds to maintain and biennially update a public municipal tree inventory, with location protections and possible grant consequences for repeated noncompliance.

title: Consumer Appliance Repair Notice Act
text: The bill requires manufacturers of household appliances sold after January 1, 2028, to disclose the expected period during which replacement parts and repair manuals will be available. The disclosure must appear online and at the point of sale. The attorney general may seek civil penalties of up to 2,500 dollars per knowing violation after providing 30 days to cure. The bill does not require manufacturers to disclose trade secrets.
summary: Requires advance disclosure of parts and repair-manual availability for household appliances sold from 2028, with point-of-sale notice, a cure period, civil penalties, and trade-secret protection.

title: Regional Flood Sensor Program
text: The bill authorizes the emergency management agency to coordinate a regional network of river and storm-drain sensors. Local governments may opt in and share readings through an open data portal. The agency must establish privacy and cybersecurity standards before collecting any device identifiers. Up to five million dollars may be appropriated annually, subject to the budget act, through fiscal year 2030.
summary: Authorizes an opt-in regional flood sensor network and open data portal, requires privacy and cybersecurity standards, and permits annual appropriations through fiscal year 2030.

title: Veteran Licensing Fee Waiver Act
text: The bill waives the initial application fee for specified occupational licenses for honorably discharged veterans and their spouses. Licensing boards may require ordinary proof of qualifications and background checks. The waiver applies once per eligible person and does not cover examination fees charged by third parties. Boards must publish application instructions by March 1, 2027.
summary: Waives one initial occupational-license application fee for eligible veterans and spouses while preserving qualification and background requirements and excluding third-party examination fees.
